newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Big markets boost W. Europe car sales in October.
newsitem.headline: Big markets boost W. Europe car sales in October.

text.p: Stronger demand in key markets France, Britain, Germany, Italy and Spain led to a 14.6 percent jump in new car registrations in western Europe in October, the European car manufacturers association (ACEA) said on Wednesday.
New passenger car registrations in the 15-nation European Union and Norway, Switzerland and Liechtenstein rose to 1,064,500 in October, up from 928,900 in the same month last year.
"The market as a whole is higher than expected...growth is stronger than expected," said James Rosenstein, director of communications at ACEA.
"But the overall trend is still well beneath the peaks that we saw in the early 1990s," he told Reuters.
So far this year, sales have risen by 7.4 percent to more than 11 million new cars in western Europe.

Unlike the situation in September, when soaring French demand for new cars before the end of a state incentives scheme led to a 12.2 percent rise in sales in western Europe, the October rise was explained by growth in several markets.
New registrations continued to grow strongly in France, up by 24.5 percent to 202,200 cars following an 85.7 percent year-on-year rise the previous month.
Rosenstein said there had been some "overhang" to the end of the incentive scheme in September as many cars bought then had not been registered until the next month.
The German market grew by 6.4 percent to 284,500 in October, the British market by 13.3 percent to 154,700 and the Italian soared by 22.9 percent to 144,500.
Rosenstein said rising consumer confidence could have boosted sales in Britain. "People are feeling more confident to buy," he said.
Of all the markets monitored by ACEA, only the Greek and the Swiss markets declined during the month.
The industry body earlier this autumn revised up its forecast for the year to overall growth of more than four percent, still well below the increase in the first 10 months.
Rosenstein said he did not know whether that figure would need to be adjusted upwards again.
The west European market has been recovering following the 16 percent drop in 1993 but is still not near its 1992 peak.

The Volkswagen group, the continent's leading carmaker, saw its registrations rise 11.5 percent to 180,900 cars in October but its market share still declined marginally to 17.0 percent from 17.5 percent last year.
France's PSA, which groups Peugeot and Citroen, also saw its share of the west European market decline, to 12.3 percent from 12.6 percent.
French rival Renault had a 20.9 percent jump in sales and its share rose to 11.0 percent from 10.5 percent.
U.S. giant Ford increased its registrations by 16.1 percent to 114,388, its share rising to 10.7 percent from 10.6.
But the General Motors group, including brands such as Opel and Saab, lost in market share to 12.1 percent from 12.5 even though its registrations rose by 10.7 percent.
